items.informal_name: Coefficient Preservation Under Injective Variable Renaming in Multivariate Polynomials
items.type:
∀ {σ : Type u_1} {τ : Type u_2} {R : Type u_4} [inst : CommSemiring R] (f : σ → τ),
  Function.Injective f →
    ∀ (φ : MvPolynomial σ R) (d : σ →₀ ℕ),
      MvPolynomial.coeff (Finsupp.mapDomain f d) ((MvPolynomial.rename f) φ) = MvPolynomial.coeff d φ
items.informal_description: For an injective function $ f : \sigma \to \tau $, a multivariate polynomial $ \varphi \in R[\sigma] $, and a finite support function $ d : \sigma \to_0 \mathbb{N} $, the coefficient of the monomial $ d.\text{mapDomain}(f) $ in the renamed polynomial $ \text{rename}(f, \varphi) $ equals the coefficient of $ d $ in $ \varphi $. This holds because injective renaming preserves monomial coefficients when variables are relabeled without collision.

  MvPolynomial.coeff (Finsupp.embDomain f d) ((MvPolynomial.rename ⇑f) φ) = MvPolynomial.coeff d φ
items.informal_description: For any injective function $ f : \sigma \to \tau $, multivariate polynomial $ \varphi \in R[\sigma] $, and finite support function $ d : \sigma \to_0 \mathbb{N} $, the coefficient of the monomial $ d.\text{embDomain}(f) $ in the renamed polynomial $ \text{rename}(f, \varphi) $ equals the coefficient of $ d $ in $ \varphi $. This equality reflects that renaming variables via an injective map preserves coefficients when monomials are adjusted by applying the map to their exponents.

For any multivariate polynomial $ \varphi \in R[\sigma] $ and finite support function $ d : \tau \to_0 \mathbb{N} $, if every monomial $ u : \sigma \to_0 \mathbb{N} $ satisfying $ u.mapDomain(f) = d $ has coefficient $ \varphi.coeff(u) = 0 $, then the coefficient of $ d $ in the renamed polynomial $ rename(f)(\varphi) $ is zero.

items.informal_description: For any function $ f : \sigma \to \tau $, variable $ i \in \sigma $, and polynomial $ p \in R[X] $, renaming the variables in the evaluation of $ p $ at $ X_i $ via $ f $ yields the same result as evaluating $ p $ at the renamed variable $ X_{f(i)} $ in $ R[\tau] $. items.type:

  (g : σ → MvPolynomial σ R),
  (MvPolynomial.rename (Prod.mk j)) (MvPolynomial.eval₂ MvPolynomial.C g p) =
    MvPolynomial.eval₂ MvPolynomial.C (fun x => (MvPolynomial.rename (Prod.mk j)) (g x)) p
items.informal_description: For any commutative semiring $ R $, types $ \sigma $ and $ \tau $, polynomial $ p \in R[\sigma] $, and variable mapping $ g : \sigma \to R[\tau] $, renaming the evaluation of $ p $ with coefficients via the constant polynomial embedding $ C $ and variables via $ g $ using the product map $ \prod.mk j $ is equivalent to evaluating $ p $ after renaming each variable in $ g $ with $ \prod.mk j $. Formally, $ \text{rename}(\prod.mk j, p.\text{eval}_2(C, g)) = p.\text{eval}_2(C, \lambda x. \text{rename}(\prod.mk j, g(x))) $.

items.informal_name: Coefficient at Degree $ |s|n $ in Product of Polynomials with Bounded Natural Degree
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u} {ι : Type w} (s : Finset ι) [inst : CommSemiring R] (f : ι → Polynomial R) (n : ℕ),
  (∀ p ∈ s, (f p).natDegree ≤ n) → (∏ i ∈ s, f i).coeff (s.card * n) = ∏ i ∈ s, (f i).coeff n
items.informal_description: For a finite set $ s $ and a function $ f $ mapping elements of $ s $ to polynomials in $ R[X] $, if each polynomial $ f(i) $ has natural degree at most $ n $, then the coefficient of the product $ \prod_{i \in s} f(i) $ at degree $ |s| \cdot n $ is equal to the product of the coefficients of each $ f(i) $ at degree $ n $. Formally, $ \operatorname{coeff}\left(\prod_{i \in s} f(i)\right)(|s| \cdot n) = \prod_{i \in s} \operatorname{coeff}(f(i))(n) $.

items.informal_name: Coefficient Formula for Product of Multivariate Polynomials
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u} {σ : Type u_1} [inst : CommSemiring R] [inst_1 : DecidableEq σ] (p q : MvPolynomial σ R) (n : σ →₀ ℕ),
  MvPolynomial.coeff n (p * q) = ∑ x ∈ Finset.antidiagonal n, MvPolynomial.coeff x.1 p * MvPolynomial.coeff x.2 q
items.informal_description: For any commutative semiring $ R $ and type $ \sigma $ with decidable equality, and for any multivariate polynomials $ p $ and $ q $ over $ R $ in variables $ \sigma $, the coefficient of a monomial $ n $ in the product $ p \cdot q $ is equal to the sum over all pairs $ (x, y) $ such that $ x + y = n $ of the product of the coefficients of $ x $ in $ p $ and $ y $ in $ q $. Formally, $ \operatorname{coeff}_n(pq) = \sum_{\substack{x + y = n\\x,y \in \operatorname{Monomials}}} \operatorname{coeff}_x(p) \cdot \operatorname{coeff}_y(q) $.

items.informal_name: Multiplicative Coefficient Property in Multivariate Polynomial Products under Monomial Order
items.type:
∀ {σ : Type u_1} {m : MonomialOrder σ} {R : Type u_2} [inst : CommSemiring R] {f g : MvPolynomial σ R} {a b : σ →₀ ℕ},
  m.toSyn (m.degree f) ≤ m.toSyn a →
    m.toSyn (m.degree g) ≤ m.toSyn b →
      MvPolynomial.coeff (a + b) (f * g) = MvPolynomial.coeff a f * MvPolynomial.coeff b g
items.informal_description: For multivariate polynomials $ f $ and $ g $ over a commutative semiring $ R $, indexed by a type $ \sigma $, and under a monomial order $ m $, if the leading monomials of $ f $ and $ g $ are less than or equal to $ a $ and $ b $ respectively, then the coefficient of $ a + b $ in the product $ f \cdot g $ is equal to the product of the coefficients of $ a $ in $ f $ and $ b $ in $ g $. That is, $ (f \cdot g)_{a + b} = f_a \cdot g_b $.

items.informal_name: Coefficient Formula for Monomial-Polynomial Multiplication in Multivariate Polynomials
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u} {σ : Type u_1} [inst : CommSemiring R] (m s : σ →₀ ℕ) (r : R) (p : MvPolynomial σ R),
  MvPolynomial.coeff (s + m) ((MvPolynomial.monomial s) r * p) = r * MvPolynomial.coeff m p
items.informal_description: For any commutative semiring $ R $, type $ \sigma $, exponent vectors $ s, m : \sigma \to₀ \mathbb{N} $, element $ r \in R $, and polynomial $ p \in R[\sigma] $, the coefficient of the exponent vector $ s + m $ in the product of the monomial $ r \cdot X^s $ and $ p $ is equal to $ r $ multiplied by the coefficient of $ m $ in $ p $. Symbolically, $ \text{coeff}(s + m, (r \cdot X^s) \cdot p) = r \cdot \text{coeff}(m, p) $.

items.informal_name: Constant Term Compatibility in Composed Algebra Maps for Polynomials
items.type:
∀ {A : Type u_3} (B : Type u_4) (C : Type u_5) [inst : CommSemiring A] [inst_1 : CommSemiring B] [inst_2 : Semiring C]
  [inst_3 : Algebra A B] [inst_4 : Algebra A C] [inst_5 : Algebra B C] [IsScalarTower A B C] (p : Polynomial A),
  (algebraMap B C) ((algebraMap A B) (p.coeff 0)) = ((Polynomial.mapAlg A C) p).coeff 0
items.informal_description: For any polynomial $ p $ over a semiring $ A $, the constant term of the polynomial obtained by applying the algebra homomorphism $ A \to C $ (induced by a scalar tower $ A \to B \to C $) to $ p $ is equal to the composition of the algebra homomorphisms $ A \to B $ and $ B \to C $ applied to the constant term of $ p $. In symbols, $ (\mathrm{algebraMap}\, B\, C) \circ (\mathrm{algebraMap}\, A\, B)(p_0) = (\mathrm{mapAlg}\, A\, C\, p)_0 $, where $ p_0 $ denotes the constant term of $ p $.

items.informal_name: Linearity Auxiliary Lemma for Polynomial-Tensor Equivalence
items.type:
∀ (R : Type u_1) (A : Type u_2) [inst : CommSemiring R] [inst_1 : Semiring A] [inst_2 : Algebra R A] (p : Polynomial R)
  (k : ℕ) (h : Decidable ¬p.coeff k = 0) (a : A),
  (if ¬p.coeff k = 0 then a * (algebraMap R A) (p.coeff k) else 0) = a * (algebraMap R A) (p.coeff k)
items.informal_description: For a polynomial $ p $ over a semiring $ R $, a natural number $ k $, and an element $ a $ of a semiring $ A $, if the coefficient of $ p $ at $ k $ is nonzero, then the conditional expression $ a \cdot \text{algebraMap}(\text{coeff}_p(k)) $ equals $ a \cdot \text{algebraMap}(\text{coeff}_p(k)) $. This equality holds trivially under the given decidable hypothesis that $ \text{coeff}_p(k) \neq 0 $.

items.informal_name: Coefficient of $ C(a) \cdot p $ at $ n $ equals $ a \cdot \text{coeff}(p, n) $
items.type: ∀ {R : Type u} {a : R} {n : ℕ} [inst : Semiring R] (p : Polynomial R), (Polynomial.C a * p).coeff n = a * p.coeff n
items.informal_description: For any polynomial $ p $ over a semiring $ R $, natural number $ n $, and element $ a \in R $, the coefficient of $ X^n $ in the product of the constant polynomial $ C(a) $ and $ p $ is equal to $ a $ multiplied by the coefficient of $ X^n $ in $ p $. Formally, $ \text{coeff}(C(a) \cdot p, n) = a \cdot \text{coeff}(p, n) $.

items.informal_name: Coefficient of Product with Constant Polynomial Equals Scalar Times Original Coefficient
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u} {σ : Type u_1} [inst : CommSemiring R] (m : σ →₀ ℕ) (a : R) (p : MvPolynomial σ R),
  MvPolynomial.coeff m (MvPolynomial.C a * p) = a * MvPolynomial.coeff m p
items.informal_description: For any commutative semiring $ R $, type $ \sigma $, monomial $ m $, element $ a \in R $, and polynomial $ p \in R[\sigma] $, the coefficient of $ m $ in the product of the constant polynomial $ a $ and $ p $ is equal to $ a $ multiplied by the coefficient of $ m $ in $ p $. That is, $ \text{coeff}(C(a) \cdot p, m) = a \cdot \text{coeff}(p, m) $.

items.informal_name: Compatibility of Scalar Multiplication with Polynomial Coefficient Mapping
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u} {S : Type v} [inst : Semiring R] {p : Polynomial R} [inst_1 : Semiring S] (f : R →+* S) (r : R),
  Polynomial.map f (r • p) = f r • Polynomial.map f p
items.informal_description: For any scalar $ r \in R $, polynomial $ p \in R[X] $, and ring homomorphism $ f : R \to S $, the polynomial obtained by first scaling $ p $ by $ r $ and then applying $ f $ to its coefficients is equal to the polynomial obtained by scaling the mapped polynomial $ p $ by $ f(r) $. In symbols, $ \text{map}_f (r \cdot p) = f(r) \cdot \text{map}_f p $.

items.type:
∀ {R : Type u} {S : Type v} [inst : Semiring R] [inst_1 : SMulZeroClass S R] (r : S) (p : Polynomial R) (n : ℕ),
  (r • p).coeff n = r • p.coeff n
items.informal_description: Let $ R $ be a semiring and $ S $ a type equipped with a scalar multiplication operation preserving zero. For any scalar $ r \in S $, polynomial $ p \in R[X] $, and natural number $ n $, the coefficient of $ X^n $ in the scalar-multiplication $ r \cdot p $ is equal to $ r \cdot \operatorname{coeff}(p, n) $.
